title: But If Not
question: What kind of faith trusts God even when He might not rescue?
blurb: Three men face the furnace with a faith that bows to no idol, whether God delivers them or not.

nodes.content: What kind of faith trusts God even when He might not rescue?

nodes.verseText: If the God whom we serve exists, then He is able to deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace and from your hand, O king. But even if He does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden statue you have set up.”

nodes.content: Their faith has two parts: God is able to deliver, AND even if He does not, they still will not worship the idol. Obedience is not conditional on rescue.

nodes.verseText: “Look!” he exclaimed. “I see four men, unbound and unharmed, walking around in the fire—and the fourth looks like a son of the gods!”
You shall have no other gods before Me.
Though He slay me, I will hope in Him. I will still defend my ways to His face.

nodes.content: Their answer to the king (v.16) is that they need no defense. They have already settled the question of whom they serve before the outcome is known.
